adhd.label: Step 1 · Jumps to Ch. 9–10: Lives of the Stars, Supernovas & Visualizing the 4th Dimension (Start Here)
adhd.brief: Starts with Sagan's most visual chapters: how dying stars cook the carbon and iron in our bodies, and how a 3D apple visiting a 2D 'Flatland' lets your brain picture curved 4-dimensional spacetime.

adhd.label: Step 2 · Jumps Back to Ch. 1: The Shores of the Cosmic Ocean & Eratosthenes' Two Sticks
adhd.brief: Visits ancient Alexandria to watch Eratosthenes measure the circumference of the entire Earth within 1% accuracy using only the shadow of an obelisk and pure geometry.

adhd.label: Step 3 · Jumps to Ch. 7: The Backbone of Night — How Ancient Ionians Discovered Science
adhd.brief: Explores how island thinkers like Thales, Democritus, and Pythagoras first realized that the universe runs on discoverable physical mechanisms rather than the whims of gods.

adhd.label: Step 4 · Jumps to Ch. 13: Who Speaks for Earth?
adhd.brief: Closes with Sagan's famous pale-blue perspective on human curiosity, survival, and our place in the cosmic ocean.
